# Whether what vibld bills for model use still covers what it costs.
#
# Every credit is a cent of model spend at the catalogue's rates, and each
# plan's margin is the gap between its price and the model spend it includes
# (docs/decisions.md L36). This compares the catalogue with two things: the
# published prices the pricing routine last read from each provider's pricing
# page (packages/ai/published-prices.json), and what Anthropic and OpenAI
# actually billed per token over the last week, through their admin APIs.
#
# It reports and never edits. A finding lands on one tracking issue, and the
# issue is closed when a run comes back clean. The catalogue is changed by a
# pull request, which is what the pricing routine opens.
name: Check model prices

on:
  schedule:
    # After midnight UTC, so yesterday's cost report is complete.
    - cron: '23 6 * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  issues: write

concurrency:
  group: check-model-prices
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  check:
    # Runs only in the private working repository. The public copy
    # (vibld/vibld) has none of the secrets or deployment environments this
    # job reads, so there it could only fail.
    if: github.repository == 'vibld/vibld-internal'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 10
    # The admin keys live beside the provider keys the builder uses.
    environment: preview
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Enable Corepack
        run: corepack enable

      - name: Setup Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: 24
          cache: pnpm

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Compare billed rates with published and billed costs
        id: check
        working-directory: apps/web
        env:
          ANTHROPIC_ADMIN_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_ADMIN_KEY }}
          OPENAI_ADMIN_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENAI_ADMIN_KEY }}
        run: node --experimental-strip-types scripts/check-model-prices.ts

      # One open issue at a time: a finding that persists is a comment on the
      # same thread, so the thread is the history of the rates drifting and
      # being corrected.
      - name: Report what it found
        if: failure() && steps.check.outcome == 'failure'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          title='Model pricing check found differences'
          report=apps/web/price-report.md
          number=$(gh issue list --state open --search "\"$title\" in:title" --json number --jq '.[0].number // empty')
          if [ -n "$number" ]; then
            gh issue comment "$number" --body-file "$report"
          else
            gh issue create --title "$title" --body-file "$report"
          fi

      - name: Close the issue once the rates agree again
        if: success()
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          title='Model pricing check found differences'
          number=$(gh issue list --state open --search "\"$title\" in:title" --json number --jq '.[0].number // empty')
          if [ -n "$number" ]; then
            gh issue comment "$number" --body-file apps/web/price-report.md
            gh issue close "$number" --reason completed
          fi

# Whether each provider still serves every model the catalogue offers, at
# the limits it records, and whether it serves a newer version of a family
# offered here.
#
# A retired id is a 404 on the next run that asks for it; a changed limit
# sizes runs wrongly; a newer version left out is a choice nobody made. The
# rules are in packages/ai/src/served-check.ts. Prices are the other
# workflow's business (check-model-prices.yml).
#
# It reports and never edits. A finding lands on one tracking issue, and the
# issue is closed when a run comes back clean. The catalogue is changed by a
# pull request.
name: Check model catalogue

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '41 6 * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  issues: write

concurrency:
  group: check-model-catalogue
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  check:
    # Runs only in the private working repository. The public copy
    # (vibld/vibld) has none of the secrets or deployment environments this
    # job reads, so there it could only fail.
    if: github.repository == 'vibld/vibld-internal'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 10
    # The same keys the builder uses; listing models spends nothing.
    environment: preview
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Enable Corepack
        run: corepack enable

      - name: Setup Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: 24
          cache: pnpm

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Compare the catalogue with what each provider serves
        id: check
        working-directory: apps/web
        env:
          ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
          OPENAI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY }}
          DEEPSEEK_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY }}
        run: node --experimental-strip-types scripts/check-model-catalogue.ts

      # One open issue at a time: a finding that persists is a comment on the
      # same thread.
      - name: Report what it found
        if: failure() && steps.check.outcome == 'failure'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          title='Model catalogue check found differences'
          report=apps/web/catalogue-report.md
          number=$(gh issue list --state open --search "\"$title\" in:title" --json number --jq '.[0].number // empty')
          if [ -n "$number" ]; then
            gh issue comment "$number" --body-file "$report"
          else
            gh issue create --title "$title" --body-file "$report"
          fi

      - name: Close the issue once the catalogue agrees again
        if: success()
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          title='Model catalogue check found differences'
          number=$(gh issue list --state open --search "\"$title\" in:title" --json number --jq '.[0].number // empty')
          if [ -n "$number" ]; then
            gh issue comment "$number" --body-file apps/web/catalogue-report.md
            gh issue close "$number" --reason completed
          fi

name: Deploy a generated preview

# Deploys a Vibld-generated project (ADR-0002: ordinary npm, no Vibld
# dependency) as its own Cloudflare Worker, purely so it can be viewed live --
# the builder shell's own preview pane only renders a local static mock and
# cannot run a model-generated project (sandbox execution is not implemented
# yet, ADR-0004). `directory` must already contain its own `wrangler.jsonc`
# naming a distinct Worker; this workflow does not invent one. Manual only.
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      directory:
        description: Path from the repo root to the generated project. Must contain its own wrangler.jsonc.
        required: true

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: deploy-preview-${{ github.event.inputs.directory }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  deploy:
    name: Build and deploy
    # Runs only in the private working repository. The public copy
    # (vibld/vibld) has none of the secrets or deployment environments this
    # job reads, so there it could only fail.
    if: github.repository == 'vibld/vibld-internal'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 10

    # Reuses the same "preview" environment apps/web deploys to -- its
    # CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN already has Workers Scripts: Edit for the whole
    # account (apps/web/README.md explains why it can't be scoped tighter),
    # which covers deploying an additional, unrelated Worker too.
    environment:
      name: preview
      url: ${{ steps.deploy.outputs.url }}

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Require Cloudflare credentials
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
        run: |
          missing=0
          [ -n "$CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN" ] || { echo "::error::CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN is not set"; missing=1; }
          [ -n "$CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID" ] || { echo "::error::CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID is not set"; missing=1; }
          if [ "$missing" -ne 0 ]; then
            echo "Add both to the \"preview\" environment (Settings -> Environments)." >&2
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Require the target directory and its wrangler.jsonc
        env:
          DIRECTORY: ${{ inputs.directory }}
        run: |
          if [ ! -f "$DIRECTORY/wrangler.jsonc" ]; then
            echo "::error::$DIRECTORY/wrangler.jsonc not found. This workflow deploys an existing generated project; it does not create one."
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Setup Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: 24

      # Plain npm, not pnpm: a generated project is deliberately not part of
      # the pnpm workspace, and is tested to build with ordinary npm commands.
      - name: Install dependencies
        working-directory: ${{ inputs.directory }}
        run: npm install --no-audit --no-fund

      - name: Build
        working-directory: ${{ inputs.directory }}
        run: npm run build

      - name: Deploy to Cloudflare Workers
        id: deploy
        shell: bash
        working-directory: ${{ inputs.directory }}
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
        run: |
          log="$RUNNER_TEMP/wrangler-deploy.log"
          npx wrangler@4.137.0 deploy | tee "$log"
          url="$(grep -oE 'https://[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.workers\.dev' "$log" | head -n 1 || true)"
          if [ -n "$url" ]; then
            echo "url=$url" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "Deployed to $url" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          else
            echo "::warning::Deploy succeeded but the URL could not be read from wrangler output"
          fi

name: Deploy marketing preview

# Manual only, like the production deploy it shadows. This exists so a change
# to vibld.com can be looked at on a real Worker before it becomes the front
# door -- there was previously no way to see the marketing site anywhere but
# production.
on:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: deploy-marketing-preview
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  deploy:
    name: Build and deploy the marketing preview
    # Runs only in the private working repository. The public copy
    # (vibld/vibld) has none of the secrets or deployment environments this
    # job reads, so there it could only fail.
    if: github.repository == 'vibld/vibld-internal'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    # The build prerenders a page per gallery style (D143).
    timeout-minutes: 15

    # The same environment the production marketing deploy uses, so the
    # Cloudflare credentials are configured in one place. This job needs only
    # the two Cloudflare values: no Resend key is synced, deliberately.
    environment:
      name: marketing
      url: ${{ steps.deploy.outputs.url }}

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Require deploy credentials
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
        run: |
          missing=0
          [ -n "$CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN" ] || { echo "::error::CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN is not set"; missing=1; }
          [ -n "$CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID" ] || { echo "::error::CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID is not set"; missing=1; }
          if [ "$missing" -ne 0 ]; then
            echo "Add both to the \"marketing\" environment (Settings -> Environments)." >&2
            echo "This deploy needs only \"Workers Scripts: Edit\" -- unlike the production deploy, it creates no DNS records." >&2
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Enable Corepack
        run: corepack enable

      - name: Setup Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: 24
          cache: pnpm

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Build
        run: pnpm --filter @vibld/marketing build

      - name: Deploy the preview
        id: deploy
        shell: bash
        working-directory: apps/marketing
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          log="$RUNNER_TEMP/wrangler-preview.log"
          pnpm dlx wrangler@4.137.0 deploy -c wrangler.preview.jsonc | tee "$log"

          # The workers.dev subdomain is account-specific, so the URL is not
          # knowable before the deploy. Wrangler prints it.
          url="$(grep -oE 'https://[a-z0-9.-]+\.workers\.dev' "$log" | head -n 1 || true)"
          if [ -z "$url" ]; then
            echo "::error::Deployed, but no workers.dev URL appeared in the output. Check that workers_dev is enabled for this account."
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "url=$url" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "Marketing preview: $url" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      # The point of this deploy is a URL a person can open, so a green upload
      # that answers nothing is not a success. The noindex check matters just
      # as much: this is a copy of vibld.com on a public hostname, and an
      # indexable copy would compete with the site it is previewing.
      #
      # The availability check retries, because the first version of this did
      # not and failed a perfectly good deploy: it asked 0.2 seconds after
      # wrangler returned and got a 404 from a workers.dev route that was not
      # serving yet. Failing on that teaches people to ignore this job, which
      # is exactly what must not happen to the noindex assertion below.
      #
      # The noindex check deliberately does not retry. Once the site answers,
      # a missing header is a real fault rather than a timing artefact.
      - name: Smoke test the preview
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          url="${{ steps.deploy.outputs.url }}"
          headers="$RUNNER_TEMP/headers.txt"

          status=000
          for attempt in $(seq 1 12); do
            status="$(curl -s -o /dev/null -D "$headers" -w '%{http_code}' --max-time 20 "$url/" || echo "000")"
            [ "$status" = "200" ] && break
            echo "attempt $attempt: $url/ answered $status, waiting for the route to serve"
            sleep 5
          done

          if [ "$status" != "200" ]; then
            echo "::error::$url/ still answered $status after about a minute. The upload succeeded, so this is the route not serving rather than a build problem."
            exit 1
          fi

          if ! grep -qi '^x-robots-tag:.*noindex' "$headers"; then
            echo "::error::$url/ is missing the noindex header. Refusing to call this preview ready: an indexable copy of vibld.com competes with the real site."
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "$url/ is live and noindex." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

name: Deploy publish service

# Manual only, like "Deploy web preview" and "Deploy sandbox service".
# Deploy this (and apply migrations/0003_publish.sql once -- see
# apps/publish/README.md) before apps/web calls /api/publish for the first
# time -- apps/web's service binding to it only routes successfully once
# "vibld-publish" actually exists.
#
# This Worker has no route of its own: vibld-preview owns
# `*.vibld-preview.dev/*` and forwards published hosts here over its PUBLISH
# service binding (ADR-0010's addendum). Published sites are only reachable
# once "Deploy sandbox service" has deployed a vibld-preview that forwards,
# so a change to how hosts are split needs both workflows run.
on:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: deploy-publish
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  deploy:
    name: Build and deploy @vibld/publish
    # Runs only in the private working repository. The public copy
    # (vibld/vibld) has none of the secrets or deployment environments this
    # job reads, so there it could only fail.
    if: github.repository == 'vibld/vibld-internal'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 10

    # Same "preview" environment apps/web, apps/marketing and apps/preview
    # already deploy from. No new Cloudflare permission needed beyond what
    # apps/preview's own token already has for the vibld-preview.dev zone
    # (ADR-0010 reuses that same zone's wildcard route, and apps/web's own
    # D1 database/R2 bucket -- see wrangler.jsonc's own comments).
    environment:
      name: preview

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Require Cloudflare credentials
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
          PUBLISH_INTERNAL_SECRET: ${{ secrets.PUBLISH_INTERNAL_SECRET }}
        run: |
          missing=0
          [ -n "$CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN" ] || { echo "::error::CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN is not set"; missing=1; }
          [ -n "$CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID" ] || { echo "::error::CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID is not set"; missing=1; }
          [ -n "$PUBLISH_INTERNAL_SECRET" ] || { echo "::error::PUBLISH_INTERNAL_SECRET is not set"; missing=1; }
          if [ "$missing" -ne 0 ]; then
            echo "Add all three to the \"preview\" environment (Settings -> Environments)." >&2
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Enable Corepack
        run: corepack enable

      - name: Setup Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: 24
          cache: pnpm

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Typecheck and test
        run: |
          pnpm --filter @vibld/publish typecheck
          pnpm --filter @vibld/publish test

      - name: Sync the internal secret to the Worker
        shell: bash
        working-directory: apps/publish
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
          PUBLISH_INTERNAL_SECRET: ${{ secrets.PUBLISH_INTERNAL_SECRET }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The value goes in on stdin so it never appears in a command line
          # or in the run log.
          printf '%s' "$PUBLISH_INTERNAL_SECRET" | pnpm dlx wrangler@4.137.0 secret put PUBLISH_INTERNAL_SECRET
          echo "Synced PUBLISH_INTERNAL_SECRET." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      # Idempotent, same as apps/web's own copy of this step -- wrangler
      # tracks what it has already applied in the database's own
      # `d1_migrations` table, so either Worker's deploy applying a pending
      # migration is enough and running it twice across both is harmless.
      # Run from apps/web, not apps/publish: the migrations directory lives
      # there (it is the shared database's own history, not this Worker's --
      # see apps/publish/wrangler.jsonc's own comment), and apps/publish has
      # no `migrations` directory of its own for wrangler to default to.
      - name: Apply D1 migrations
        shell: bash
        working-directory: apps/web
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
        run: pnpm dlx wrangler@4.137.0 d1 migrations apply vibld-control-plane --remote

      - name: Deploy to Cloudflare Workers
        shell: bash
        working-directory: apps/publish
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
        run: |
          pnpm dlx wrangler@4.137.0 deploy
          {
            echo "Deployed vibld-publish (<slug>.vibld-preview.dev)."
            echo "Published sites reach it through vibld-preview, which forwards their hosts: run **Deploy sandbox service** too if its last deploy predates the change you are shipping."
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

name: Deploy sandbox service

# Manual only, like "Deploy web preview". Deploy this before apps/web
# whenever PREVIEW_INTERNAL_SECRET changes or apps/preview itself changes --
# apps/web's service binding to it only routes successfully once
# "vibld-preview" actually exists.
on:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: deploy-sandbox-service
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  deploy:
    name: Build and deploy @vibld/preview
    # Runs only in the private working repository. The public copy
    # (vibld/vibld) has none of the secrets or deployment environments this
    # job reads, so there it could only fail.
    if: github.repository == 'vibld/vibld-internal'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 15

    # Same "preview" environment apps/web and apps/marketing already deploy
    # from -- see apps/preview/README.md for exactly which token scopes it
    # needs beyond what's already there (DNS: Edit on vibld-preview.dev).
    environment:
      name: preview

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Require Cloudflare credentials
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
          PREVIEW_INTERNAL_SECRET: ${{ secrets.PREVIEW_INTERNAL_SECRET }}
        run: |
          missing=0
          [ -n "$CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN" ] || { echo "::error::CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN is not set"; missing=1; }
          [ -n "$CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID" ] || { echo "::error::CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID is not set"; missing=1; }
          [ -n "$PREVIEW_INTERNAL_SECRET" ] || { echo "::error::PREVIEW_INTERNAL_SECRET is not set"; missing=1; }
          if [ "$missing" -ne 0 ]; then
            echo "Add all three to the \"preview\" environment (Settings -> Environments)." >&2
            echo "The Cloudflare token needs \"Workers Scripts: Edit\" (already covers this account) and \"DNS: Edit\" on the vibld-preview.dev zone, for the wildcard route." >&2
            exit 1
          fi

      # The Sandbox SDK builds the container image at deploy time; GitHub's
      # ubuntu-24.04 runners ship Docker preinstalled, so this only ever
      # fails if that ever changes.
      - name: Require Docker
        run: docker info > /dev/null

      - name: Enable Corepack
        run: corepack enable

      - name: Setup Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: 24
          cache: pnpm

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Typecheck and test
        run: |
          pnpm --filter @vibld/preview typecheck
          pnpm --filter @vibld/preview test

      - name: Sync the internal secret to the Worker
        shell: bash
        working-directory: apps/preview
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
          PREVIEW_INTERNAL_SECRET: ${{ secrets.PREVIEW_INTERNAL_SECRET }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The value goes in on stdin so it never appears in a command line
          # or in the run log.
          printf '%s' "$PREVIEW_INTERNAL_SECRET" | pnpm dlx wrangler@4.137.0 secret put PREVIEW_INTERNAL_SECRET
          echo "Synced PREVIEW_INTERNAL_SECRET." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      # Signs and verifies share links (docs/decisions.md L10,
      # worker/share-token.ts). Optional, unlike PREVIEW_INTERNAL_SECRET
      # above: an unset value means /api/preview/share answers "not
      # configured" (a 503) rather than the whole deploy failing, the same
      # "additive, not load-bearing" rule PREVIEW_INTERNAL_SECRET itself
      # follows on apps/web's own deploy.
      - name: Sync the share secret to the Worker
        shell: bash
        working-directory: apps/preview
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
          PREVIEW_SHARE_SECRET: ${{ secrets.PREVIEW_SHARE_SECRET }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -n "$PREVIEW_SHARE_SECRET" ]; then
            printf '%s' "$PREVIEW_SHARE_SECRET" | pnpm dlx wrangler@4.137.0 secret put PREVIEW_SHARE_SECRET
            echo "Synced PREVIEW_SHARE_SECRET." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          else
            echo "PREVIEW_SHARE_SECRET not set -- /api/preview/share stays unconfigured on this deploy." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          fi

      # Building the container image can take several minutes on a cold
      # cache -- longer than apps/web's or apps/marketing's plain Worker
      # deploys, which upload source only.
      - name: Deploy to Cloudflare Workers
        shell: bash
        working-directory: apps/preview
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
        run: |
          pnpm dlx wrangler@4.137.0 deploy
          echo "Deployed vibld-preview (*.vibld-preview.dev)" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

name: Deploy marketing site

# On every push to main that changes what vibld.com is built from, and by
# hand (Chris, D106). It was manual only, to avoid redeploying on unrelated
# merges; the paths below do that instead, and a manual-only deploy left
# vibld.com a day and a half behind main on 2026-09-30.
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - apps/marketing/**
      # The site reads the style presets, the model catalogue, the template
      # catalog and the backgrounds from packages/ai, plans and prices from
      # these Worker modules (apps/marketing/turbo.json), and the examples.
      - packages/ai/**
      - packages/brand/**
      - packages/security-headers/**
      - apps/web/worker/entitlement.ts
      - apps/web/worker/signup-credit.ts
      - apps/web/worker/stripe-client.ts
      - apps/web/worker/referral.ts
      - apps/web/worker/model-access.ts
      - examples/**
      - pnpm-lock.yaml
      - .github/workflows/deploy-marketing.yml
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: deploy-marketing
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  deploy:
    name: Build and deploy vibld.com
    # Runs only in the private working repository. The public copy
    # (vibld/vibld) has none of the secrets or deployment environments this
    # job reads, so there it could only fail.
    if: github.repository == 'vibld/vibld-internal'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    # The build prerenders a page per gallery style (D143).
    timeout-minutes: 15

    # Credentials live on this environment rather than the repository, so
    # they are reachable only from a job that names it, and any protection
    # rule configured on it (a required reviewer) gates the run before a
    # single step executes.
    environment:
      name: marketing
      url: ${{ steps.deploy.outputs.url }}

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          # Full history, so postbuild.ts can date each page in sitemap.xml
          # from the last commit that touched it. A shallow clone knows one
          # commit, and postbuild then leaves lastmod out rather than stamp
          # every page with the same date.
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Require deploy credentials
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
        run: |
          missing=0
          [ -n "$CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN" ] || { echo "::error::CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN is not set"; missing=1; }
          [ -n "$CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID" ] || { echo "::error::CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID is not set"; missing=1; }
          if [ "$missing" -ne 0 ]; then
            echo "Add both to the \"marketing\" environment (Settings -> Environments)." >&2
            echo "The Cloudflare token needs \"Workers Scripts: Edit\" and \"DNS: Edit\" on the vibld.com zone -- the routes in wrangler.jsonc create that zone's records on first deploy -- and \"D1: Edit\" on the account, for the roadmap's migrations." >&2
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Enable Corepack
        run: corepack enable

      - name: Setup Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: 24
          cache: pnpm

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Build
        run: pnpm --filter @vibld/marketing build

      # TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY is a Worker secret, not a build input, so it is
      # pushed separately from the deploy -- the same reasoning as the
      # model-key sync in deploy-web-preview.yml.
      #
      # It is optional: it is not in "Require deploy credentials" above, and
      # without it the roadmap (worker/roadmap.ts) refuses a browser's first
      # vote rather than the deploy failing (docs/decisions.md L29) -- so it
      # is synced only when present, the same `[ -n ... ]` pattern
      # deploy-web-preview.yml uses for the model keys.
      - name: Sync Worker secrets
        shell: bash
        working-directory: apps/marketing
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
          TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY: ${{ secrets.TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The value goes in on stdin so it never appears in a command line
          # or in the run log.
          if [ -n "$TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY" ]; then
            printf '%s' "$TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY" | pnpm dlx wrangler@4.137.0 secret put TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY
            echo "Synced TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          else
            echo "TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY not set -- /roadmap refuses a browser's first vote on this deploy." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          fi

      # Idempotent -- wrangler tracks applied migrations in the database's own
      # `d1_migrations` table and only runs what is new. Runs before the
      # deploy itself so a Worker never goes live expecting a table a
      # migration this same push added hasn't created yet: the same step, for
      # the same reason, as deploy-web-preview.yml's for apps/web. The job's
      # `if: github.repository == 'vibld/vibld-internal'` guard covers it.
      - name: Apply D1 migrations
        shell: bash
        working-directory: apps/marketing
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
        run: pnpm dlx wrangler@4.137.0 d1 migrations apply vibld-marketing-roadmap --remote

      - name: Deploy to Cloudflare Workers
        id: deploy
        shell: bash
        working-directory: apps/marketing
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
        run: |
          log="$RUNNER_TEMP/wrangler-deploy.log"
          pnpm dlx wrangler@4.137.0 deploy | tee "$log"
          url="$(grep -oE 'https://vibld\.com' "$log" | head -n 1 || true)"
          if [ -n "$url" ]; then
            echo "url=$url" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          echo "Deployed vibld-marketing (vibld.com, www.vibld.com)" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      # A green deploy only says the upload worked, not that the site is
      # answering. This used to warn and pass, for the days when a freshly
      # routed domain could still be propagating; vibld.com has been routed
      # since, so a site that does not answer is a failed deploy (internal PR 59).
      # A few tries, a few seconds apart, cover the edge picking up the new
      # version.
      - name: Smoke test the deployment
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          for attempt in 1 2 3 4 5; do
            status="$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --max-time 20 https://vibld.com/ || echo "000")"
            [ "$status" = "200" ] && break
            sleep 6
          done
          if [ "$status" != "200" ]; then
            echo "::error::https://vibld.com/ answered $status after five tries."
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "https://vibld.com/ is live." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      - name: Notify IndexNow
        working-directory: apps/marketing
        run: pnpm indexnow

name: Deploy web preview

# Manual only. An automatic deploy on every push to main would redeploy on
# every merge; the builder shell is a review aid, not something users depend
# on being current. Run this from the Actions tab to refresh the preview.
on:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: deploy-web-preview
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  deploy:
    name: Build and deploy the builder shell
    # Runs only in the private working repository. The public copy
    # (vibld/vibld) has none of the secrets or deployment environments this
    # job reads, so there it could only fail.
    if: github.repository == 'vibld/vibld-internal'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 10

    # Credentials live on this environment rather than the repository, so they
    # are reachable only from a job that names it, and any protection rule
    # configured on it (a required reviewer) gates the run before a single
    # step executes. Repository-level secrets of the same name still work as a
    # fallback, so moving them is not a breaking change.
    environment:
      name: preview
      url: ${{ steps.deploy.outputs.url }}

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Require Cloudflare credentials
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
        run: |
          missing=0
          [ -n "$CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN" ] || { echo "::error::CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN is not set"; missing=1; }
          [ -n "$CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID" ] || { echo "::error::CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID is not set"; missing=1; }
          if [ "$missing" -ne 0 ]; then
            echo "Add both to the \"preview\" environment (Settings -> Environments)." >&2
            echo "The token needs \"Workers Scripts: Edit\" and nothing more." >&2
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Enable Corepack
        run: corepack enable

      - name: Setup Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: 24
          cache: pnpm

      # The invite gate (apps/web/worker/access-gate.ts). Unset means
      # invite-only, which is the launch state and the safe default, and the
      # Worker opens only on the exact string `open`.
      #
      # This decides; "Sync the access mode" below writes. They are two steps
      # because `wrangler secret put` creates a new Worker version and
      # deploys it immediately, and the very first secret this job syncs is
      # VIBLD_PLATFORM_ADMINS itself. A check that ran alongside the write
      # would publish a broken admin list, lock out the admins who could
      # have fixed it, and only then fail the run: a refusal that arrives
      # after the damage is not a refusal.
      #
      # The decision lives in apps/web/scripts/access-preflight.ts rather
      # than here, and imports the Worker's own `parseAccessMode`,
      # `parsePlatformAdmins` and `normaliseEmail`. Written as shell it was a
      # second implementation of those three rules in a language with
      # different semantics, and every time the two disagreed the deploy was
      # the more generous one, which is the direction that ships the outage.
      #
      # Placed after Setup Node because it needs the pinned Node 22 to strip
      # types, and before Install dependencies because both modules it reaches
      # are dependency-free. It needs no Cloudflare credentials and writes
      # nothing.
      - name: Check who can get in, before any secret is written
        shell: bash
        working-directory: apps/web
        env:
          VIBLD_ACCESS_MODE: ${{ secrets.VIBLD_ACCESS_MODE }}
          VIBLD_PLATFORM_ADMINS: ${{ secrets.VIBLD_PLATFORM_ADMINS }}
          CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY: ${{ secrets.CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY }}
        run: node --experimental-strip-types scripts/access-preflight.ts

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      # CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY is not sensitive -- Clerk designs it to ship in
      # the client bundle -- but it lives alongside CLERK_SECRET_KEY on this
      # environment rather than as a repository var, so both are set in one
      # place. Vite only inlines VITE_-prefixed env vars into the build, and
      # only at build time; an unset key here means ClerkRoot renders nothing
      # rather than the app failing to build or boot (see src/auth/clerk.tsx).
      - name: Build
        env:
          VITE_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY: ${{ secrets.CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY }}
        run: pnpm --filter @vibld/web build

      # Model keys are Worker secrets, not build inputs, so they are pushed
      # separately from the deploy. Doing it here rather than by hand means
      # the key is pasted in exactly one place -- the `preview` environment --
      # instead of once for CI and again in a terminal.
      #
      # Only a key that is actually configured is pushed: an unset secret is
      # an empty string here, and writing that would replace a working Worker
      # secret with nothing.
      - name: Sync model credentials to the Worker
        shell: bash
        working-directory: apps/web
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
          ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
          DEEPSEEK_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY }}
          OPENAI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY }}
          VIBLD_MODEL_POLICY: ${{ secrets.VIBLD_MODEL_POLICY }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          # The provider the deployment selects, read from the committed
          # config rather than guessed, so this fails before a deploy that
          # would leave the live site without the key it needs.
          provider="$(node --experimental-strip-types scripts/wrangler-var.ts VIBLD_PROVIDER anthropic)"
          echo "wrangler.jsonc selects: $provider"

          put() {
            # The value goes in on stdin so it never appears in a command line
            # or in the run log.
            printf '%s' "$2" | pnpm dlx wrangler@4.137.0 secret put "$1"
          }

          case "$provider" in
            deepseek) required=DEEPSEEK_API_KEY ;;
            openai)   required=OPENAI_API_KEY ;;
            *)        required=ANTHROPIC_API_KEY ;;
          esac
          if [ -z "${!required}" ]; then
            echo "::error::$required is not set on the 'preview' environment, but wrangler.jsonc selects $provider. Add it before deploying, or the live site falls back to the deterministic fake."
            exit 1
          fi

          # `[ -n "$x" ] && put ...` would abort the whole step under `set -e`
          # the moment one key is unconfigured, which is the normal case.
          if [ -n "$ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" ]; then
            put ANTHROPIC_API_KEY "$ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"
          fi
          if [ -n "$DEEPSEEK_API_KEY" ]; then
            put DEEPSEEK_API_KEY "$DEEPSEEK_API_KEY"
          fi
          if [ -n "$OPENAI_API_KEY" ]; then
            put OPENAI_API_KEY "$OPENAI_API_KEY"
          fi
          # Who may use which model. A secret rather than a var because it
          # names people and this repository is public. Unset means no policy:
          # everyone may use whatever the deployment can serve.
          if [ -n "$VIBLD_MODEL_POLICY" ]; then
            put VIBLD_MODEL_POLICY "$VIBLD_MODEL_POLICY"
          fi
          echo "Synced the model credentials that are configured." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      # Shared with @vibld/preview's own copy of the same value (see
      # deploy-sandbox-service.yml) -- apps/web's /api/preview uses it to
      # authenticate to that Worker over the PREVIEW service binding.
      # Optional here: an unset value means /api/preview answers "not
      # configured" rather than the whole deploy failing (docs/decisions.md
      # L7-L11 is additive to a deployment that already works without it).
      - name: Sync the preview service secret to the Worker
        shell: bash
        working-directory: apps/web
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
          PREVIEW_INTERNAL_SECRET: ${{ secrets.PREVIEW_INTERNAL_SECRET }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -n "$PREVIEW_INTERNAL_SECRET" ]; then
            printf '%s' "$PREVIEW_INTERNAL_SECRET" | pnpm dlx wrangler@4.137.0 secret put PREVIEW_INTERNAL_SECRET
            echo "Synced PREVIEW_INTERNAL_SECRET." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          else
            echo "PREVIEW_INTERNAL_SECRET not set -- /api/preview stays unconfigured on this deploy." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          fi

      # ADR-0010. Shared with @vibld/publish's own copy of the same value --
      # apps/web's /api/publish uses it to authenticate to that Worker over
      # the PUBLISH service binding. Optional, same rule as the preview
      # secret above: unset means /api/publish answers "not configured"
      # rather than the whole deploy failing.
      - name: Sync the publish service secret to the Worker
        shell: bash
        working-directory: apps/web
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
          PUBLISH_INTERNAL_SECRET: ${{ secrets.PUBLISH_INTERNAL_SECRET }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -n "$PUBLISH_INTERNAL_SECRET" ]; then
            printf '%s' "$PUBLISH_INTERNAL_SECRET" | pnpm dlx wrangler@4.137.0 secret put PUBLISH_INTERNAL_SECRET
            echo "Synced PUBLISH_INTERNAL_SECRET." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          else
            echo "PUBLISH_INTERNAL_SECRET not set -- /api/publish stays unconfigured on this deploy." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          fi

      # Stripe billing (docs/decisions.md L12-L15). Optional, same as
      # PREVIEW_INTERNAL_SECRET above: unset means handlePlan's budget gate
      # and /api/billing/* answer "not configured" rather than the whole
      # deploy failing -- billing is additive to a deployment that already
      # works without it.
      - name: Sync Stripe credentials to the Worker
        shell: bash
        working-directory: apps/web
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
          STRIPE_SECRET_KEY: ${{ secrets.STRIPE_SECRET_KEY }}
          STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET: ${{ secrets.STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -n "$STRIPE_SECRET_KEY" ]; then
            printf '%s' "$STRIPE_SECRET_KEY" | pnpm dlx wrangler@4.137.0 secret put STRIPE_SECRET_KEY
            echo "Synced STRIPE_SECRET_KEY." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          else
            echo "STRIPE_SECRET_KEY not set -- billing stays unconfigured on this deploy." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          fi
          if [ -n "$STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET" ]; then
            printf '%s' "$STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET" | pnpm dlx wrangler@4.137.0 secret put STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET
            echo "Synced STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          else
            echo "STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET not set -- /api/stripe/webhook stays unconfigured on this deploy." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          fi

      # Stock photo search (D176): Unsplash first, Pexels when Unsplash finds
      # none or refuses. Optional, and either alone works: with neither, a
      # build with no uploaded media paints its images in CSS as before.
      #
      # Unlike the secrets above, a key removed from the environment is
      # deleted from the Worker too: a Worker keeps a secret no deploy
      # mentions, so taking a key out of `preview` would otherwise leave the
      # Worker searching with it. Wrangler confirms the delete itself in CI.
      - name: Sync stock photo keys to the Worker
        shell: bash
        working-directory: apps/web
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
          UNSPLASH_ACCESS_KEY: ${{ secrets.UNSPLASH_ACCESS_KEY }}
          PEXELS_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.PEXELS_API_KEY }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The Worker's secret names, read once. A failure to read them
          # fails the step: a key removed here must not stay live there.
          secrets="$(pnpm dlx wrangler@4.137.0 secret list --format json | node -e '
            let raw = "";
            process.stdin.on("data", (chunk) => (raw += chunk));
            process.stdin.on("end", () => {
              for (const secret of JSON.parse(raw)) console.log(secret.name);
            });
          ')"
          for name in UNSPLASH_ACCESS_KEY PEXELS_API_KEY; do
            if [ -n "${!name}" ]; then
              printf '%s' "${!name}" | pnpm dlx wrangler@4.137.0 secret put "$name"
              echo "Synced $name." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            elif grep -qxF "$name" <<< "$secrets"; then
              pnpm dlx wrangler@4.137.0 secret delete "$name"
              echo "$name removed from the preview environment, so deleted from the Worker." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            else
              echo "$name not set -- no photos from that service on this deploy." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            fi
          done

      # The GitHub App that pushes a checkpoint to a user's repository
      # (internal issue 13). Optional, same rule as every secret above: unset means
      # /api/github/* answers "not configured" rather than the deploy
      # failing.
      #
      # VIBLD_GITHUB_PRIVATE_KEY is the .pem GitHub generated for the App,
      # pasted whole into the environment secret (BEGIN/END lines and all).
      # It never travels any other way: not by email, not through a chat, and
      # not into this repository. `printf %s` rather than a heredoc so the
      # newlines inside it survive, and it is piped straight into wrangler so
      # it is never an argument any process listing could show.
      # Before anything replaces a live secret, not after.
      #
      # `wrangler secret put` writes straight to the running Worker, so a
      # malformed or mismatched pair checked afterwards is already installed:
      # the deploy then fails and looks safely blocked while every push on the
      # live site is broken by the credentials this run just wrote. Checking
      # first means a bad pair stops the run having changed nothing, and only
      # credentials that answered GitHub are synced.
      #
      # It also says what the App may do, which the key being present does
      # not: a read-only App looks configured from every angle the rest of
      # this workflow can see and answers 422 on every push.
      #
      # Skipped when there is no App to ask about, like every other optional
      # secret here.
      - name: Check the GitHub App before syncing its credentials
        working-directory: apps/web
        env:
          VIBLD_GITHUB_APP_ID: ${{ secrets.VIBLD_GITHUB_APP_ID }}
          VIBLD_GITHUB_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.VIBLD_GITHUB_PRIVATE_KEY }}
        run: node --experimental-strip-types scripts/check-github-app.ts

      - name: Sync the GitHub App credentials to the Worker
        shell: bash
        working-directory: apps/web
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
          VIBLD_GITHUB_APP_ID: ${{ secrets.VIBLD_GITHUB_APP_ID }}
          VIBLD_GITHUB_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.VIBLD_GITHUB_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          VIBLD_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID: ${{ secrets.VIBLD_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID }}
          VIBLD_GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET: ${{ secrets.VIBLD_GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET }}
          VIBLD_GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET: ${{ secrets.VIBLD_GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -n "$VIBLD_GITHUB_APP_ID" ] && [ -n "$VIBLD_GITHUB_PRIVATE_KEY" ]; then
            printf '%s' "$VIBLD_GITHUB_APP_ID" | pnpm dlx wrangler@4.137.0 secret put VIBLD_GITHUB_APP_ID
            printf '%s' "$VIBLD_GITHUB_PRIVATE_KEY" | pnpm dlx wrangler@4.137.0 secret put VIBLD_GITHUB_PRIVATE_KEY
            echo "Synced the GitHub App credentials." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          else
            echo "VIBLD_GITHUB_APP_ID/VIBLD_GITHUB_PRIVATE_KEY not both set -- pushing to GitHub stays unconfigured on this deploy." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          fi
          # The OAuth half, which is what lets somebody connect a repository
          # in the first place. Synced separately because it gates a
          # different thing: without it a deployment can still push on a
          # binding it already has, it just cannot make new ones.
          if [ -n "$VIBLD_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID" ] && [ -n "$VIBLD_GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET" ]; then
            printf '%s' "$VIBLD_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID" | pnpm dlx wrangler@4.137.0 secret put VIBLD_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID
            printf '%s' "$VIBLD_GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET" | pnpm dlx wrangler@4.137.0 secret put VIBLD_GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET
            echo "Synced the GitHub OAuth credentials." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          else
            echo "VIBLD_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID/VIBLD_GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET not both set -- connecting a repository stays unconfigured on this deploy." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          fi
          # The webhook secret, which is the whole of the authentication on
          # /api/github/webhook: no session reaches that route. Unset means
          # the route answers 503 and a merged pull request goes on being
          # reported as open, which is a stale readout rather than a broken
          # push.
          if [ -n "$VIBLD_GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET" ]; then
            printf '%s' "$VIBLD_GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET" | pnpm dlx wrangler@4.137.0 secret put VIBLD_GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET
            echo "Synced the GitHub webhook secret." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          else
            echo "VIBLD_GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET not set -- pull request state stays unreported on this deploy." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          fi

      # L44's nightly provider-balance check. Optional, same rule as every
      # secret above: unset means the check still runs and logs, it just
      # cannot send. Cloudflare Secrets are per-Worker, not shared.
      - name: Sync the Resend key to the Worker
        shell: bash
        working-directory: apps/web
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
          RESEND_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.RESEND_API_KEY }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -n "$RESEND_API_KEY" ]; then
            printf '%s' "$RESEND_API_KEY" | pnpm dlx wrangler@4.137.0 secret put RESEND_API_KEY
            echo "Synced RESEND_API_KEY." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          else
            echo "RESEND_API_KEY not set -- the L44 balance check still runs but cannot send an alert." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          fi

      # The welcome credit's cohort cutoff (signup-credit.ts). Not secret, but
      # synced the same way as the values above so it is configured in one
      # place rather than by hand against a live Worker after every deploy.
      #
      # Without it the credit is granted to nobody: there is no safe default,
      # because any cutoff early enough to catch genuinely new accounts also
      # catches every account that already exists. So "not set" is reported
      # loudly here rather than passed over, since a silent no-op is exactly
      # what it would otherwise look like.
      #
      # Format is a full ISO instant with a timezone, e.g.
      # 2026-09-13T00:00:00Z. Anything else is refused by signupCohortStart
      # and grants nobody anything, so it is checked here too rather than
      # discovered as an absence of credits later.
      - name: Sync the signup credit cutoff to the Worker
        shell: bash
        working-directory: apps/web
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
          VIBLD_SIGNUP_CREDIT_FROM: ${{ secrets.VIBLD_SIGNUP_CREDIT_FROM }}
          VIBLD_SIGNUP_CREDIT_USD_CENTS: ${{ secrets.VIBLD_SIGNUP_CREDIT_USD_CENTS }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -z "$VIBLD_SIGNUP_CREDIT_FROM" ]; then
            echo "::warning::VIBLD_SIGNUP_CREDIT_FROM is not set on the 'preview' environment, so no new account will receive the welcome credit. Set it to the ISO instant the offer starts, e.g. 2026-09-13T00:00:00Z."
            echo "Signup credit: OFF (no cohort cutoff configured)." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          elif ! printf '%s' "$VIBLD_SIGNUP_CREDIT_FROM" | grep -qE '^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}(:[0-9]{2}(\.[0-9]{1,3})?)?(Z|[+-][0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2})$'; then
            echo "::error::VIBLD_SIGNUP_CREDIT_FROM is not a full ISO instant with a timezone. The Worker would refuse it and grant nobody anything. Expected something like 2026-09-13T00:00:00Z."
            exit 1
          elif ! day="$(date -u -d "${VIBLD_SIGNUP_CREDIT_FROM:0:10}" +%Y-%m-%d 2>/dev/null)" \
            || [ "$day" != "${VIBLD_SIGNUP_CREDIT_FROM:0:10}" ]; then
            # The shape can be right and the day still not exist. The Worker
            # checks this too, but only after the value is already deployed:
            # catching it here is the difference between a failed deploy and
            # a green one that silently grants nobody anything.
            echo "::error::VIBLD_SIGNUP_CREDIT_FROM names a day that does not exist (${VIBLD_SIGNUP_CREDIT_FROM:0:10}). The Worker would refuse it and grant nobody anything."
            exit 1
          else
            printf '%s' "$VIBLD_SIGNUP_CREDIT_FROM" | pnpm dlx wrangler@4.137.0 secret put VIBLD_SIGNUP_CREDIT_FROM
            echo "Signup credit: accounts created from $VIBLD_SIGNUP_CREDIT_FROM." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          fi
          # Optional. Unset means the default, 0 cents since D163 (the credit
          # is retired). An existing Worker secret stays until replaced, so
          # set this to 0 rather than deleting it to retire the grant.
          # `secret put` publishes a new version of the Worker already live,
          # before this run deploys its own code, so retire it on a deploy
          # that follows one carrying the webhook's own check of this switch
          # (`signupCreditOpen`, D163); the old webhook pays any open offer.
          if [ -n "$VIBLD_SIGNUP_CREDIT_USD_CENTS" ]; then
            printf '%s' "$VIBLD_SIGNUP_CREDIT_USD_CENTS" | pnpm dlx wrangler@4.137.0 secret put VIBLD_SIGNUP_CREDIT_USD_CENTS
            echo "Signup credit amount: ${VIBLD_SIGNUP_CREDIT_USD_CENTS}c." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          fi

      # Platform admins (docs/decisions.md L4) and the Clerk secret key
      # `/api/admin/*` uses to resolve an admin-typed email into the Clerk
      # user id the ledger keys on (clerk-lookup.ts). Optional, same rule as
      # every secret above: unset means `/api/admin/*` answers "not
      # configured" rather than the whole deploy failing -- the admin credit
      # tool is additive to a deployment that already works without it.
      - name: Sync admin credentials to the Worker
        shell: bash
        working-directory: apps/web
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
          VIBLD_PLATFORM_ADMINS: ${{ secrets.VIBLD_PLATFORM_ADMINS }}
          CLERK_SECRET_KEY: ${{ secrets.CLERK_SECRET_KEY }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -n "$VIBLD_PLATFORM_ADMINS" ]; then
            printf '%s' "$VIBLD_PLATFORM_ADMINS" | pnpm dlx wrangler@4.137.0 secret put VIBLD_PLATFORM_ADMINS
            echo "Synced VIBLD_PLATFORM_ADMINS." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          else
            echo "VIBLD_PLATFORM_ADMINS not set -- no admin grants on this deploy." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          fi
          if [ -n "$CLERK_SECRET_KEY" ]; then
            printf '%s' "$CLERK_SECRET_KEY" | pnpm dlx wrangler@4.137.0 secret put CLERK_SECRET_KEY
            echo "Synced CLERK_SECRET_KEY." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          else
            echo "CLERK_SECRET_KEY not set -- /api/admin/* stays unconfigured on this deploy." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          fi

      # The write. Its refusal moved out to a check before any secret is
      # touched (see "Check who can get in" above): `wrangler secret put`
      # deploys a new Worker version immediately, so a step that validated
      # here would have already published the value it then refused.
      - name: Sync the access mode
        shell: bash
        working-directory: apps/web
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
          VIBLD_ACCESS_MODE: ${{ secrets.VIBLD_ACCESS_MODE }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ "${VIBLD_ACCESS_MODE:-}" = "open" ]; then
            printf 'open' | pnpm dlx wrangler@4.137.0 secret put VIBLD_ACCESS_MODE
            echo "Access: OPEN. Anybody who signs up can use the builder." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            exit 0
          fi
          printf 'invite' | pnpm dlx wrangler@4.137.0 secret put VIBLD_ACCESS_MODE
          echo "Access: INVITE ONLY. Admins can issue invites from the builder." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      # The key the admin panel's provider keys are encrypted under in D1
      # (D127, D132). Created once, here, and never replaced: a new one
      # would leave every stored key unreadable, so this writes only when
      # the Worker has none, and fails rather than guesses when it cannot
      # tell. Only secret names are listed; no value is ever readable.
      - name: Create the provider-key encryption key, once
        shell: bash
        working-directory: apps/web
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          listed="$(pnpm dlx wrangler@4.137.0 secret list --format json)"
          # 0: present, 1: absent, anything else: the list could not be read.
          set +e
          printf '%s' "$listed" | node scripts/has-secret.mjs VIBLD_KEY_ENCRYPTION_KEY
          found=$?
          set -e
          case "$found" in
            0)
              echo "VIBLD_KEY_ENCRYPTION_KEY is set; left as it is." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
              ;;
            1)
              openssl rand -base64 32 | tr -d '\n' | pnpm dlx wrangler@4.137.0 secret put VIBLD_KEY_ENCRYPTION_KEY
              echo "Created VIBLD_KEY_ENCRYPTION_KEY: the panel can store provider keys." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
              ;;
            *)
              echo "::error::Could not read the Worker's secret names, so VIBLD_KEY_ENCRYPTION_KEY was left alone."
              exit 1
              ;;
          esac

      # Idempotent -- wrangler tracks applied migrations in the database's own
      # `d1_migrations` table and only runs what is new. Runs before the
      # deploy itself so a Worker never goes live expecting a table a
      # migration this same push added hasn't created yet. This step's own
      # absence was a real production bug: 0002_billing.sql and
      # 0003_publish.sql sat unapplied for two days after their PRs merged,
      # and every /api/plan call failed with "Usage accounting is
      # unavailable" until this was caught and applied by hand.
      - name: Apply D1 migrations
        shell: bash
        working-directory: apps/web
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
        run: pnpm dlx wrangler@4.137.0 d1 migrations apply vibld-control-plane --remote

      - name: Deploy to Cloudflare Workers
        id: deploy
        shell: bash
        working-directory: apps/web
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
        run: |
          log="$RUNNER_TEMP/wrangler-deploy.log"
          pnpm dlx wrangler@4.137.0 deploy | tee "$log"

          # A custom domain route (apps/web/wrangler.jsonc's "routes") makes
          # wrangler disable the workers.dev preview URL by default -- its
          # output then lists the domain under "Deployed ... triggers" as
          # "  app.vibld.com (custom domain)" instead of printing a
          # https://*.workers.dev line at all. Prefer that when present;
          # fall back to the workers.dev line for a deployment with no
          # custom domain configured.
          url="$(sed -n 's/^[[:space:]]*\([A-Za-z0-9.-]*\) (custom domain)$/https:\/\/\1/p' "$log" | head -n 1 || true)"
          if [ -z "$url" ]; then
            url="$(grep -oE 'https://[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.workers\.dev' "$log" | head -n 1 || true)"
          fi
          if [ -n "$url" ]; then
            echo "url=$url" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "Deployed the builder shell to $url" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          else
            echo "::warning::Deploy succeeded but the URL could not be read from wrangler output"
          fi

      # A green deploy only says the upload worked. This asserts what the
      # running Worker actually does over HTTP, which is the layer where the
      # "Load failed" bug lived while every source check stayed green.
      - name: Smoke test the deployment
        env:
          VIBLD_SMOKE_ORIGIN: ${{ steps.deploy.outputs.url }}
        run: node scripts/smoke.mjs

name: CI

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  quality:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    # vibld.com prerenders a page per gallery style (D143), 1,300+ pages,
    # which put the build past ten minutes on its own.
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Enable Corepack
        run: corepack enable

      - name: Setup Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: 24
          cache: pnpm

      - name: Install dependencies
        # Frozen: a lockfile that does not match package.json is a failure, not
        # something to paper over. The permissive install hid real drift --
        # packages/core was missing from the lockfile across four merges and
        # CI stayed green throughout.
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Format check
        run: pnpm format:check

      - name: House style
        run: pnpm check:style

      - name: Typecheck
        run: pnpm typecheck

      # vibld.com's tests build the site themselves and prerender a page per
      # gallery style (D143), each a request React Router fails after ten
      # seconds. Beside every other package's tests, on a runner's four
      # cores, a page took longer and the build failed (internal PR 356). So they run
      # on their own, after the rest.
      - name: Test
        run: pnpm test --filter='!@vibld/marketing'

      - name: Test vibld.com
        run: pnpm test --filter=@vibld/marketing

      # The repository scripts are not a workspace package, so turbo's test
      # task never reaches them. Their tests run here instead.
      - name: Script tests
        run: pnpm test:scripts

      # Every app's production build, which nothing above runs: typecheck
      # passes on code Vite then refuses to bundle, and until this step a
      # break like that reached main and was first seen by a deploy.
      #
      # The Clerk key is a placeholder. The build only embeds it, and a real
      # one would put an instance identifier in logs for no gain.
      #
      # Not vibld.com: its tests above ran its build script, postbuild
      # included, and a second prerender would only repeat it.
      - name: Build
        env:
          VITE_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY: pk_test_placeholder
        run: pnpm build --filter='!@vibld/marketing'

  # The eval stub reported a project accepted that stopped at
  # "vite: not found" (internal PR 59). Writing one case out and building it is the
  # only check that sees that. One case: they share a manifest, and each
  # build is a registry install. In a container, as the bakeoff runs
  # candidates, so the path a model's code takes is exercised on every pull
  # request.
  #
  # A job of its own, with its own time: one candidate may take up to 13
  # minutes at its worst (install, build, and the container's start and
  # removal), more than the quality job's limit allows after everything
  # else it runs (internal PR 237 review). The script is given what is left of the
  # job's time, less a reserve, so a slow registry is reported as a
  # candidate it had no time for, not cut off without a word.
  eval-build:
    name: Build what the eval stub accepts
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 25
    steps:
      - name: Note when the job started
        run: echo "JOB_STARTED=$(date +%s)" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Enable Corepack
        run: corepack enable

      - name: Setup Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: 24
          cache: pnpm

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      # Docker Hub refuses unauthenticated pulls past a limit that runners
      # share by address, which failed this job before any of it ran
      # (D187). Each Docker Hub image this job uses is pulled from
      # mirror.gcr.io and tagged with its Docker Hub name, so the build and
      # `docker run` find it locally and never ask Docker Hub. Setting the
      # daemon's `registry-mirrors` was tried first, and the pull still
      # went to Docker Hub.
      - name: Pull Docker Hub images through mirror.gcr.io
        run: |
          for image in node:24-bookworm-slim; do
            docker pull --quiet "mirror.gcr.io/library/$image"
            docker tag "mirror.gcr.io/library/$image" "docker.io/library/$image"
          done

      - name: Write one case out and build it
        run: |
          VIBLD_EVAL_OUT="$RUNNER_TEMP/eval-stub" pnpm --filter @vibld/eval run eval --case coffee-roaster
          minutes=$(( (25 * 60 - ($(date +%s) - JOB_STARTED)) / 60 - 2 ))
          [ "$minutes" -ge 1 ] || minutes=1
          node --experimental-strip-types packages/eval/bin/build-candidates.ts "$RUNNER_TEMP/eval-stub" "$minutes" --container node:24-bookworm-slim

  # vibld under docker compose, with no Cloudflare account (D126): the
  # image builds, the three Workers start under workerd, and the owner
  # signs in. A preview's sandbox is a container on the runner's Docker
  # (D137); starting one is left to the end-to-end check (D122).
  docker:
    name: Docker
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 25
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Setup Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: 24

      # Docker Hub refuses unauthenticated pulls past a limit that runners
      # share by address, which failed this job before any of it ran
      # (D187). Each Docker Hub image the Dockerfile and the VPS compose
      # file name is pulled from mirror.gcr.io and tagged with its Docker
      # Hub name, so the build and compose find it locally and never ask
      # Docker Hub. Setting the
      # daemon's `registry-mirrors` was tried first, and the pull still
      # went to Docker Hub.
      - name: Pull Docker Hub images through mirror.gcr.io
        run: |
          for image in docker:28-cli node:24-bookworm-slim traefik:v3; do
            docker pull --quiet "mirror.gcr.io/library/$image"
            docker tag "mirror.gcr.io/library/$image" "docker.io/library/$image"
          done

      - name: Start it
        env:
          # Not a secret: this copy lives for the length of the job.
          VIBLD_OWNER_PASSWORD: ci-owner-password-123
          # A local model (D124) with no server behind it: listing it needs
          # none, and building with it is not what this job checks.
          VIBLD_LOCAL_MODEL: ci-local-model
        run: |
          printf 'VIBLD_OWNER_PASSWORD=%s\nOPENAI_API_KEY=sk-not-a-real-key\nVIBLD_PROVIDER=openai\nVIBLD_LOCAL_BASE_URL=http://localhost:11434/v1\nVIBLD_LOCAL_MODEL=%s\n' "$VIBLD_OWNER_PASSWORD" "$VIBLD_LOCAL_MODEL" > .env
          docker compose up --build --detach

      - name: Sign in
        env:
          VIBLD_OWNER_PASSWORD: ci-owner-password-123
          VIBLD_LOCAL_MODEL: ci-local-model
        run: node docker/smoke.mjs 900

      - name: Logs
        if: always()
        run: docker compose logs --no-color | tail -n 300

      # The same image as a container host runs it (D141, render.yaml): one
      # port from PORT, no Docker socket, the builder alone.
      - name: Start it on one port with the sandbox off
        env:
          VIBLD_OWNER_PASSWORD: ci-owner-password-123
        run: |
          docker compose down
          docker run --detach --name vibld-one-port -p 10000:10000 \
            -e VIBLD_SANDBOX=off -e PORT=10000 \
            -e VIBLD_OWNER_PASSWORD -e OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-not-a-real-key \
            vibld

      - name: Sign in on one port
        env:
          VIBLD_OWNER_PASSWORD: ci-owner-password-123
          VIBLD_SANDBOX: 'off'
          PORT: '10000'
        run: node docker/smoke.mjs 600

      - name: Logs on one port
        if: always()
        run: docker logs vibld-one-port 2>&1 | tail -n 200 || true

      # As infrastructure/vps runs it on a server (D141): the proxy ends TLS
      # and the Workers listen on 127.0.0.1 only. The domains are made up,
      # so no certificate is issued and the proxy's own one is accepted.
      - name: Start it behind the server's proxy
        run: |
          docker rm --force vibld-one-port
          printf 'VIBLD_DOMAIN=build.vibld.test\nVIBLD_PREVIEW_DOMAIN=vibld-preview.test\nCF_DNS_API_TOKEN=not-a-real-token\n' >> .env
          docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f infrastructure/vps/compose.yml up --detach
          # The server's firewall rules apply, and applying them twice adds
          # nothing.
          sudo infrastructure/vps/firewall.sh
          sudo infrastructure/vps/firewall.sh
          sudo iptables -S DOCKER-USER
          sudo ip6tables -S DOCKER-USER
          [ "$(sudo iptables -S DOCKER-USER | grep -c DROP)" = 2 ]
          [ "$(sudo ip6tables -S DOCKER-USER | grep -c DROP)" = 2 ]

      - name: Sign in behind the server's proxy
        env:
          VIBLD_OWNER_PASSWORD: ci-owner-password-123
          VIBLD_DOMAIN: build.vibld.test
          VIBLD_PREVIEW_DOMAIN: vibld-preview.test
        run: |
          node docker/smoke.mjs 900
          # Through the proxy, as a browser would: https, the builder's own
          # origin, and a session cookie marked Secure.
          resolve='--resolve build.vibld.test:443:127.0.0.1 --resolve 8080-x-y.vibld-preview.test:443:127.0.0.1'
          curl --silent --show-error --insecure $resolve --dump-header headers.txt --output /dev/null \
            --request POST https://build.vibld.test/api/owner/session \
            --header 'content-type: application/json' --header 'origin: https://build.vibld.test' \
            --data "{\"password\":\"$VIBLD_OWNER_PASSWORD\"}"
          grep -i '^HTTP/.* 200' headers.txt
          grep -i '^set-cookie:.*; Secure' headers.txt > /dev/null
          echo 'the owner signs in through the proxy'
          # Any other host goes to the preview Worker, which knows no such
          # preview.
          status=$(curl --silent --insecure $resolve --output /dev/null --write-out '%{http_code}' https://8080-x-y.vibld-preview.test/)
          echo "an unknown preview answers $status"
          [ "$status" -ge 400 ] && [ "$status" -lt 500 ]
          # And nothing answers on the Workers' ports from outside the server.
          ip=$(hostname -I | awk '{ print $1 }')
          for port in 8787 8788 8789; do
            if curl --silent --max-time 5 "http://$ip:$port/" > /dev/null; then
              echo "a Worker answers on $ip:$port"; exit 1
            fi
          done
          echo "the Workers' ports are closed to $ip"
          # A client cannot pick its own address: wrong passwords, each with a
          # different forged CF-Connecting-IP, still run into the limit.
          limited=no
          for n in $(seq 1 30); do
            status=$(curl --silent --insecure $resolve --output /dev/null --write-out '%{http_code}' \
              --request POST https://build.vibld.test/api/owner/session \
              --header 'content-type: application/json' --header 'origin: https://build.vibld.test' \
              --header "cf-connecting-ip: 198.51.100.$n" --data '{"password":"wrong"}')
            if [ "$status" = 429 ]; then limited=yes; break; fi
          done
          [ "$limited" = yes ]
          echo "forged addresses are throttled after $n attempts"

      - name: Logs behind the server's proxy
        if: always()
        run: docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f infrastructure/vps/compose.yml logs --no-color | tail -n 300

  # The marketing template is deliberately outside the pnpm workspace: it has
  # to install and build on its own, with npm and no Vibld packages, because
  # that is what a user who exports it will do. Building it here is the only
  # way that claim stays true.
  template:
    name: Marketing template
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 10
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: templates/marketing
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Setup Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: 24
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: templates/marketing/package-lock.json

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Typecheck
        run: npm run typecheck

      - name: Test
        run: npm test

      # A user who exports the template runs this next, so it has to work.
      - name: Build
        run: npm run build

  # The Luminous template sits outside the workspace for the same reason as
  # the marketing template: a user who exports it installs and builds it with
  # npm alone, so that is how CI builds it too.
  luminous-template:
    name: Luminous template
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 10
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: templates/luminous
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Setup Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: 24
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: templates/luminous/package-lock.json

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Typecheck
        run: npm run typecheck

      - name: Test
        run: npm test

      # A user who exports the template runs this next, so it has to work.
      - name: Build
        run: npm run build

# Tripline landing page

A single-page marketing site for Tripline, a fictional service that monitors a company's external attack surface: the servers, subdomains, certificates and DNS records anyone on the internet can see. The page has a hero with a sample findings console, a coverage overview, a setup timeline, three pricing tiers with a monthly and annual toggle, an FAQ and a contact form.

The product, prices and data on the page are illustrative. The contact form validates input and simulates a send, but it does not transmit anything; the page says so next to the form.

## Built with

- React 19 and TypeScript, bundled by Vite
- Tailwind CSS v4, configured in `src/styles.css` through the `@tailwindcss/vite` plugin (there is no `tailwind.config.js`)
- shadcn/ui components written into `src/components/ui/` on top of the `radix-ui` package (accordion, tabs, button, input, label, textarea)
- lucide-react for icons and Motion (`motion/react`) for animation

## Requirements

- Node.js 20.19 or newer (22 LTS works well)
- npm, which ships with Node.js

No account, API key or external service is needed. The only network request at runtime is the Google Fonts stylesheet for Space Grotesk and IBM Plex Sans; if it fails, the page falls back to system fonts.

## Install

```bash
npm install
```

## Run in development

```bash
npm run dev
```

Vite prints a local address, usually http://localhost:5173. Edits reload in the browser.

## Check types

```bash
npm run typecheck
npm run lint
```

`typecheck` runs the TypeScript compiler without emitting files. `lint` runs the same compiler with unused locals and parameters reported as errors.

## Build for production

```bash
npm run build
```

This type-checks the project and writes a static site to `dist/`. Preview the built output with:

```bash
npm run preview
```

The contents of `dist/` can be served by any static host.

## Project layout

```
src/
  main.tsx            entry point, imports styles.css
  App.tsx             page composition and the plan-to-contact hand-off
  styles.css          fonts, Tailwind, colour and type tokens
  types.ts            shared types
  lib/utils.ts        cn() class merge helper
  lib/motion.ts       shared easing curve
  components/         page sections
  components/ui/      shadcn/ui components
```

## Changing the design

Colours live as CSS custom properties on `:root` in `src/styles.css` and are exposed to Tailwind through `@theme inline`, so `bg-primary` or `text-muted-foreground` always read the token. The type scale (`text-display`, `text-title`, `text-lead` and so on) is declared in the `@theme` block in the same file.

The acid yellow `--primary` is reserved for the trial buttons and the focus ring. Keep it that way if you add sections, or it stops standing out.

## Hooking up the form

`src/components/Contact.tsx` validates fields and then waits 900ms in `handleSubmit`. Replace that wait with a request to your own endpoint, and change the demonstration notice and success text to match.
